Add assertions for internal assumptions
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList methods that take an index assuming its validated.
Every command path in getResponse routes through
parseIndex first, but this is not stated anywhere in the
code.

If a caller skips validation, the failure would surface as
an IndexOutOfBoundsException from inside ArrayList, or silently as
wrong behaviour. Nothing in the code distinguishes incorrect user
input from a broken internal contract.

Assert the assumptions the code already guarantees: the index
preconditions in TaskList, the matching postcondition on
parseIndex, a non-null collection in the constructor, a non-null
command after parsing, and a fully assigned task after decoding a
save line.

Use assertions rather than exceptions because these conditions can
only be false if the code itself is wrong. Invalid user input is a
normal occurrence and continues to throw MeowMeowException, which
is caught and shown to the user. An assertion that fires instead
indicates a defect.

Enable assertions for the run task via applicationDefaultJvmArgs,
since the JVM disables them by default and they would otherwise
never execute. Confirmed by temporarily inverting one assertion
and observing the resulting AssertionError.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use streams for filtering and joining
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList.findOccurringOn and findByKeyword each declare a result
list, loop over every task, and add the ones that match.
Storage.save follows the same shape to build its output string.
In all three, a one-line filter or mapping is spread across six
lines of accumulator bookkeeping.

The loop mechanics obscure the operation being performed, and the
mutable accumulator is an implementation detail unrelated to what
the method means.

Replace these loops with stream pipelines.

Use streams for readability rather than speed. On lists this small
a sequential stream is, if anything, marginally slower than an
enhanced for loop; the gain is that filter and map name the
operation directly. Collect with toCollection(ArrayList::new)
rather than toList() so the declared return types are preserved,
and append the line separator inside the map in Storage.save so
the save file keeps its trailing newline, which joining with a
delimiter would have dropped.

Leave the numbered-list loops in Ui unchanged. Their index is part
of the output, and the IntStream.range equivalent reads worse than
the loop it would replace.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract duplicated numbered-list rendering in UI
commitResults.messageBody:
formatList, formatTasksOn and formatMatches each build a numbered
list of tasks with their own StringBuilder and index loop. The
three loops are identical apart from the heading they start from.

Changing how tasks are numbered means finding and editing three
separate places, and each public method mixes deciding what to
show with the mechanics of rendering it.

Extract the shared loop into a private formatNumberedTasks helper
taking the heading and the tasks, and have the three methods
delegate to it.

Keep the empty-list handling in the callers rather than moving it
into the helper. Each has a different empty case: a replacement
message for two of them, and a heading followed by a note for the
date listing. Folding those in would need another parameter and
would blur what the helper does.

Output is unchanged in all three cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove duplicated command-word splitting in Parser
commitResults.messageBody:
parseCommand, parseCommandWord and parseArguments each split the
trimmed input on whitespace into at most two parts. The regex and
the decision to stop at two parts are repeated in all three.

Changing how the command word is separated from its arguments
would mean editing three places, and the bare split expression
gives a reader no indication of what the two parts represent.

Delegate parseCommand to parseCommandWord, which already returns
the first word, and extract the remaining split into a private
splitCommandAndArguments helper shared by parseCommandWord and
parseArguments.

Prefer delegation over the helper where it applies. parseCommand
needs only the command word, so routing it through an existing
public method removes the duplication outright rather than moving
it into a shared private one.

Behaviour is unchanged and ParserTest passes without
modification.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the task indentation constant for UI
commitResults.messageBody:
formatTaskMessage, formatAdded and formatRemoved each prefix the
task with a two-space string literal. The literal appears three
times with nothing to say what it is for.

Changing the indentation of a displayed task means finding three
identical literals and knowing that all three mean the same
thing, which nothing in the code states.

Extract the literal into a TASK_INDENT constant and use it at all
three sites.

Output is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract shared add and remove confirmation in UI
commitResults.messageBody:
formatAdded and formatRemoved produce the same three-line message
and differ only in the opening sentence. The indented task line
and the closing count sentence are duplicated between them.

The count sentence in particular is user-facing text repeated
verbatim, so the two confirmations can drift apart through an
edit to one of them.

Extract the shared shape into a private formatTaskCountMessage
helper taking the opening sentence, the task and the new count,
and have both methods delegate to it.

Output is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject duplicate tasks when adding
commitResults.messageBody:
Nothing prevents the same task being added twice. Typing todo read
book repeatedly appends an identical entry each time, leaving a
list with entries a user cannot tell apart.

Deleting the wrong copy then becomes easy, and the save file
accumulates redundant records that persist across sessions.

Reject an add when the list already holds an equivalent task, and
report it as an ordinary error message.

Compare tasks with a named isDuplicateOf method rather than by
overriding equals. Two tasks that differ only in completion status
are not equal, yet a finished task should still count as a
duplicate of a new one with the same description, so equality is
the wrong concept. Keeping the rule in its own method also leaves
ArrayList behaviour untouched.

Tasks of different types are never duplicates, and descriptions
are compared ignoring case. Deadlines and events additionally
compare their dates, which required giving TaskDateTime an equals
and hashCode: without them the comparison fell back to reference
identity and never matched.

Extract the shared add, save and confirm sequence out of the three
add cases into a private addTask method, so the duplicate check
lives in one place rather than three.

commitResults.messageTitle: Credit code reused from the JavaFX tutorial
Organise classes into packages by responsibility
commitResults.messageBody:
All seventeen classes sit in a single meowmeow package, so the
structure gives no indication of which classes handle parsing,
storage, the task model, or the user interface.

Move them into parser, storage, task and ui subpackages, leaving
Launcher, MeowMeow and MeowMeowException at the top level.

Keep Launcher at the top level so the mainClass entry in
build.gradle is unaffected, and update the fx:controller reference
in MainWindow.fxml, which is a string the refactoring tool does not
rewrite.

No behaviour changes; all tests pass unmodified.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restore explicit imports after the package move
commitResults.messageBody:
Moving classes into subpackages left IntelliJ's generated imports
in place, and in two files those were collapsed into wildcard
form. Import ordering also diverged between files, since before
the move there were no cross-package imports to be consistent
about.

The coding standard requires explicit imports and a consistent
ordering.

Replace the wildcards with explicit imports and apply one ordering
across every file.

No behaviour changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle more invalid input and accept day names
commitResults.messageBody:
Several kinds of invalid input are accepted or reported badly. An
event can start after it ends. A deadline can be set in the past.
A repeated /by or /from is silently ignored, leaving the extra
text to fail later as an unreadable date. And any unexpected
exception escaping getResponse leaves the window accepting input
and doing nothing, with the error visible only in the console.

Reject an event whose start is not before its end, reject a
deadline or event start that has already passed, reject a repeated
delimiter, and show a message in the dialog when an unexpected
exception occurs. Also accept mon to sun, and the full day names,
as a date meaning the next occurrence of that day.

Put the ordering check in the Event constructor, so an invalid
event cannot be built by any path. Put the past checks in Parser
instead: Storage rebuilds tasks from the save file, and a deadline
saved last week is legitimately in the past, so a constructor
check would reject it, count the line as corrupted and silently
drop the task.

Only the event start is compared against the present, since the
constructor already guarantees the start precedes the end, so a
future start implies a future end. The on command is deliberately
left unchecked, because searching past dates is its purpose.

Catch Exception rather than Throwable in the GUI handler, so an
AssertionError still propagates and stays visible in development.

Day names resolve relative to today and are stored as the concrete
date they resolved to, so a saved task keeps its date rather than
drifting forward on each launch.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject dates that do not exist in the calendar
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskDateTime builds its input formatters with
DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern, which resolves leniently by default.
A day outside its month is silently adjusted to the nearest valid
one, so 2099-02-30 becomes 28 February and 2099-04-31 becomes 30
April. Both are accepted and saved as a date the user never asked
for.

Someone who mistypes a date gets a task on a different day with no
indication that anything was changed, which is worse than an
outright rejection.

Resolve input dates strictly, so a day outside its month is
rejected and reported like any other unreadable date.

Switch the year field in the input patterns from yyyy to uuuu.
Strict resolution treats yyyy as a year-of-era, which needs an era
field the input never supplies, so every parse would fail instead.
uuuu is the proleptic year and resolves on its own. The output
formatters keep yyyy, since they only ever format.

Leave fromStorage unchanged: it parses with the ISO formatters,
which already resolve strictly. A real 29 February in a leap year
is still accepted.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover date parsing and the new validation rules
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskDateTime had no tests at all, despite being the class with the
most input formats and the most recent changes. The validation
rules added for the previous increment were also untested: a
deadline in the past, an event starting in the past, an event
starting after it ends, and a repeated delimiter.

Untested parsing is where a silent behaviour change hides, as the
lenient date resolution showed.

Add a TaskDateTimeTest covering each accepted input format, day
names, strict calendar resolution, the past comparison, equality
across precisions, and the storage round trip. Extend ParserTest
with the rejection paths for deadlines and events.

Assert that a day name resolves to a future date with the right
day of week, rather than to a fixed date, so the tests do not
depend on the day they are run. Use 2099 dates where a valid
future date is needed, which keeps the expected output literal at
the cost of a test suite that expires in 2099.

Include a case where the description contains the text /to, which
pins the decision to count the /to delimiter only after /from.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for storage, commands and output formatting
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage, CommandType and Ui have no automated tests. Storage is
the largest gap: it is the only class that touches the filesystem,
and a fault there loses a user's saved tasks rather than producing
a wrong answer on screen.

Add a StorageTest covering the missing-file case, a save and load
round trip across all three task types including a completed one,
a file mixing valid and corrupted lines, blank-line handling, and
creation of a missing parent directory. Add small tests for
CommandType.fromString and for the Ui formatting methods.

Use JUnit's TempDir for the storage tests so each one works in its
own directory and the real save file is never touched. The
injected field cannot be private, which is a framework
requirement rather than an oversight.

Leave the JavaFX classes untested. Launcher, Main, MainWindow and
DialogBox need a running toolkit and are verified manually.

Extract command handlers out of getResponse
commitResults.messageBody:
getResponse is 65 lines. Each switch case carries its own parsing,
mutation and saving, so the method mixes routing a command with
carrying it out.

Move the body of each multi-statement case into a private method
and turn the switch into an expression that returns the result.

Drop the default branch. All eleven CommandType constants are now
listed, so a switch expression over the enum is exhaustive without
one. Adding a new command becomes a compile error at this switch
rather than a runtime message no user should ever see.

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Split record parsing by task type
commitResults.messageBody:
parseLine is 49 lines. It validates the fields every record shares,
constructs a task of one of three types with its own field checks,
and applies the done flag, all in one method.

It also signals a malformed record two ways: returning null when a
field is missing, and throwing when a date cannot be read. A reader
has to follow both paths to work out when a line gets skipped.

Extract the shared field check and the per-type construction into
private methods, and have each of them throw on a malformed record,
so the existing catch is the single place a bad line becomes null.

Drop the assertion that a task was assigned. The switch expression
either yields a task or throws, so the compiler now guarantees what
the assertion was checking at runtime.

commitResults.messageTitle: Improve dialog layout and styling
commitResults.messageBody:
Each message reserves a 99-pixel square for a photograph, the
scroll pane draws its default grey background, and the dialog text
is fixed-width so that an ASCII cat in the welcome message stays
aligned. The window also cannot be resized usefully: its children
are placed at absolute coordinates, so the layout stays at 400 by
600 whatever the user does to the frame.

Shrink the avatar, give each message a coloured bubble so the two
speakers are distinguishable at a glance, and add a stylesheet
that frames the window in blue with a pale blue chat area.
Reposition every child with anchors so the layout follows the
window, and let the scroll pane size its content to the viewport.

Drop the ASCII cat from the welcome message and return the dialog
text to the platform's proportional font. The avatar already
identifies the speaker, so the drawing was duplicating it while
forcing every message into a fixed-width font. This reverses the
font choice made when the GUI was first built, and CONTRIBUTORS.md
is updated to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: List the available commands in the welcome message
commitResults.messageBody:
A new user sees only a greeting on startup and has to guess what
to type or go to the user guide. The command list exists in the
code, but only in the error shown after a wrong guess.

Show the full command list and the accepted date formats in the
welcome message.

Move the list into a single constant in Ui and have the unknown
command error use it too, so the two places that show it cannot
drift apart.
